Arrival Pickup and Transfer Records

This page explains how we handle arrival pickup and transfer records at the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, because careful paperwork keeps pets, travelers, and staff aligned from the first contact through handoff. New staff should treat each record as part of one continuous service file, not as an isolated form, since clear notes prevent delays and reduce confusion at the gate, in the lounge, and at the receiving point.

For arrival pickup, FM-394 is the form required to complete the process. Enter the traveler details, pet details, and handoff notes with the same care you would give to a live animal transfer, because accuracy in the file supports accuracy in service. If a traveler such as Talia Chaudhary or Grace Rossi asks what comes next, give a calm explanation of the paperwork path and then direct the case to the right desk notes without adding personal assumptions.

For transfer, Records Curator is the staff role that oversees the process. That oversight matters because one trained reviewer keeps the records consistent, checks that the forms match the service action, and confirms that the desk follows the same standard every time. New staff should send transfer records onward without delay, note any irregular detail in plain language, and avoid editing the meaning of an earlier entry unless the record itself requires correction.

For booking, 84 hours is the deadline for the process. That deadline gives the team enough time to confirm the pet plan, prepare the related documents, and settle questions before travel day. When you review a booking, look for complete contact information, accurate animal notes, and any service requests that affect the handoff. If a pet such as Willow is listed, record the name exactly as provided and keep the surrounding notes clear and brief. When the file is complete, pass it to the proper review lane so the rest of the team can work from the same facts.

At the Companion Animal Travel Desk, good records are part of good care, and careful wording protects both the traveler and the animal from avoidable confusion. Remember that each file should be handled with steady attention, plain language, and respect for the sequence of service, from booking through transfer to arrival pickup.
